headline: Korean medical AI company Lunit has agreed with the U.S. laboratory services firm Discovery Life Sciences to build its cancer-tissue analysis software into the lab's testing for drug trials.
score_reason: Pool 4 kept: announced on 12 Oct 2026 and the article matches the headline; no terms or named drugmakers were given.
importance_line: AI tissue analysis would move from reading cancer samples in diagnosis to the laboratories that support drug trials, which could matter to trial researchers and drugmakers and later to patients, but no financial terms, participating drugmakers or starting volumes were disclosed, and the gain in consistency is the companies' own claim.
summary: Korea Biomedical Review reports that Lunit, a Korean company whose AI software reads images of cancer tissue, announced on Monday 12 Oct 2026 an agreement with Discovery Life Sciences, a U.S. laboratory services provider that, according to Lunit, supports more than 350 active clinical trial programs, to build Lunit SCOPE, its AI pathology software, into Discovery's tissue processing and biomarker analysis (the measuring of biological signs of disease or drug response) for participating drug and biotech clients. The companies say this could give researchers more consistent and reproducible tissue data, but Lunit did not disclose financial terms, name the drugmakers taking part or say how many research programs will use the software at first.
notes: Read in full via Korea Biomedical Review (fulltext). Figures about Discovery (350 active programs, 2,000 programs over 25 years) are attributed to Lunit in the article.
